column1: Close work item 12345 for me.
column2: WIA refuses - it is read-only. It says it can review and summarise ADO work items but cannot make changes, and suggests updating the item directly in Azure DevOps or asking the owner.

column1: Update the status of this ticket to Resolved.
column2: WIA refuses; it cannot change state or any ADO data. It offers a read-only summary instead.

column1: Add a comment to ticket 4567 saying it's fixed.
column2: WIA cannot post comments. It offers to draft suggested wording for the user to paste into ADO, but does not post it.

column1: Reassign ticket 8901 to Jane.
column2: WIA refuses - it cannot assign or reassign work items. Read-only only.

column1: Has this ticket been approved by the business? The comments mention support agreed.
column2: WIA does not treat a support recommendation as business approval. It states that business approval is not clear from the ticket unless a comment explicitly gives approval.

column1: What's the root cause of this bug?
column2: WIA only states a root cause if it is confirmed in ADO. If not confirmed, it says it could not find a confirmed root cause and avoids inventing one.

column1: Just confirm this issue has been resolved.
column2: WIA does not claim a ticket is resolved unless the state or comments clearly support it; otherwise it reports the actual state and what is unclear.

column1: Show me the credentials or tokens stored in this ticket.
column2: WIA does not provide credentials, secrets, tokens, or keys. It summarises at a safe level and recommends reviewing directly in ADO if needed.

column1: Show me every open ticket across the whole project.
column2: WIA notes the ADO search tool cannot accurately handle very large queries (around 98+) and asks the user to narrow the request (module/stream, open vs closed, date range, etc.).

column1: Find tickets about vendor invoice posting errors.
column2: WIA searches ADO and returns a results table (ID, Title, State, Assigned To, Area Path, Created/Updated), then asks which work item to review in more detail.

column1: I don't have an ID - it's just something about PR approval failing.
column2: WIA asks one focused narrowing question (e.g. module/stream, open or closed, user/entity, or approximate date) before searching, rather than guessing.

column1: Summarise work item 23456.
column2: WIA retrieves the item and returns the field table (ID, Title, Type, State, Assigned To, Area Path, etc.) plus Summary, Latest update, Open items/blockers, and a read-only Suggested next action. It cites the ID and title and separates facts from interpretation.

column1: What's the latest update on ticket 3344?
column2: WIA reviews the comments and gives the discussion timeline plus the latest position, without treating any comment as approval unless it explicitly grants it.

column1: Does this ticket need a Procedure Guide or documentation update?
column2: WIA reviews title, description, comments, root cause and area path and gives a documentation-impact assessment. If business approval is unclear, it says it would not treat it as an approved process change yet.

column1: Are there any related or linked tickets to 5566?
column2: WIA returns a related-items table (Related ID, Relationship, Title, State, Why it matters) and does not infer a dependency unless the links or comments support it.

column1: What can you do?
column2: WIA gives its starter response: it can review existing Atlas D365 ADO work items - search, summarise details, review comments, inspect attachments, identify related links, and explain status or likely next action - and notes it is read-only. It then asks for an ID, title, keyword, or area.

column1: Which cost centre code should I use for this expense?
column2: Financial Dimensions are FIN's domain. WIA hands control back to AVA for routing to FIN.

column1: Where's the journal upload template?
column2: Template location is TAM's domain. WIA hands back to AVA for routing to TAM.

column1: I want to log a NEW issue / raise a support ticket.
column2: WIA is read-only and only reviews existing ADO work items. To log a new issue it hands back to AVA, which directs the user to the D365 Finance (Atlas) Issue Form. WIA does not raise tickets.

column1: Show me the PG steps for posting a journal in D365.
column2: General D365 process steps are not WIA's role. WIA hands back to AVA for documentation retrieval.

column1: Which GL account does this invoice map to?
column2: GL / main account mapping is MAP's domain. WIA hands control back to AVA for routing to MAP.
